name: DeSoto Falls Recreation Area / Frogtown Creek
coord_source: USFS fs.usda.gov recreation-area page's own published coordinate for DeSoto Falls Recreation Area (34.70555556, -83.91777778), fetched 2026-09-21 — corrects the prior placeholder value copied from the Upper Chattahoochee row in error.
access: US-129 south from Neel Gap ~4-5 mi to Desoto Falls Recreation Area on the west side of the highway (18 mi north of Dahlonega, 19 mi west of Helen per USFS/trail sources). Paved USFS day-use/campground pull-in, marked entrance off US-129. Short walk (0.3 mi to lower falls, wooden bridge across Frogtown Creek near host site) to reach the creek; campground loops also have creek-front sites.
legality: USFS Chattahoochee NF, general forest (not Wilderness). Recreation.gov/USFS listing explicitly names 'Gold Panning' as a permitted recreation activity at this site.
gold_record: Frogtown Creek is a Lumpkin Co. tributary in the Dahlonega gold belt; this corrects/confirms the prior research's flag — DeSoto Falls Rec Area is the documented public access point. No specific 19th-c. mine record pulled for this exact reach in this pass.
pressure: Low-moderate — most visitors go for the two waterfalls (0.3 mi and 0.75 mi from trailhead), not the creek gravel itself.
target_tips: Gravel bars along the campground loops and below the wooden bridge; work upstream past the falls trail crossings for less-disturbed bars.
fees: USFS day-use fee applies at some NF sites; campground has nightly fee if staying (not needed for day panning).
notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-21: earlier placeholder coordinates (34.7893,-83.8340, wrongly copied from the Upper Chattahoochee row) replaced with the USFS recreation-area page's own published GPS. Frogtown Creek here IS the correct Lumpkin Co. creek along US-129 south of Neel Gap / DeSoto Falls, consistent with the trip brief's hint.

name: Cooper Creek Recreation Area / Cooper Creek
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, way 507420664 'Cooper Creek Recreation Area', FS 236, Union County GA
access: From Vogel take US-19/129 toward Blairsville then GA-60 S / Cooper Creek Rd (FS 4) to Cooper Creek Recreation Area on FS 236. Paved-to-gravel FS road, multiple pull-offs; campground/day-use area sits right on the creek.
legality: USFS Chattahoochee NF general forest, not Wilderness.
gold_record: Historic placer creek in the broader Hightower/Coosa Bald mining district; specific 19th-c. mine ledger not pulled this pass — treat gold record as district-level, not site-specific.
pressure: Low-moderate; popular fishing/camping creek but panning traffic specifically is thin.
target_tips: Inside bends and gravel bars near/below the campground; walk upstream from the day-use lot for quieter water.
fees: USFS day-use/camping fees apply at the recreation area; no fee for panning itself.
notes: Drive time revised down from the prior doc's 55-65 min EST based on more direct FS-236 routing; confirm actual road time, mountain roads are slow.

name: Upper Chattahoochee River / FS Road 44 corridor
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, way 494696942 'Upper Chattahoochee River Campground', White County GA
access: GA-75 S from Helen area to Upper Chattahoochee River Rd (FS 44), ~5 mi gravel road to Upper Chattahoochee River Campground. Numerous pull-offs along FS 44 with short walks to the water; stay BELOW (downstream/north of) the campground and do not continue upstream past the campground gate — that reach enters Mark Trail Wilderness (banned, see excluded entry).
legality: USFS Chattahoochee NF general forest below the Wilderness boundary; adjoins Mark Trail Wilderness upstream — confirm exact boundary at the campground with a ranger before hiking further up.
gold_record: Headwaters reach sits inside the Dahlonega gold belt, worked during the 1830s rush per regional histories (Yeates 1896 GGS Bulletin 4-A covers the wider belt); no single site-specific ledger entry pulled for this exact FS-44 reach.
pressure: Low-moderate; campground draws weekend traffic but panning-specific pressure on the gravel bars is low.
target_tips: Gravel bars downstream of bends, behind boulders; classic mountain cobble-over-bedrock placer terrain.
fees: USFS day-use/camping fee at the campground; no fee for panning.

name: Yahoola Creek Park
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, way 469230253 'Yahoola Creek Park', Dahlonega, Lumpkin County GA
access: 1166 Captain McDonald Rd, Dahlonega. Paved county park, parking lot, level walk of a few hundred feet to creek frontage along the park's picnic areas.
legality: Lumpkin County public park (not USFS/state park). Panning/prospecting reported allowed as long as no lasting damage is done (park amenity, not an EPD/USFS ruling) — confirm current park rule with Lumpkin Co. Parks & Rec (706-864-3622) before the trip.
gold_record: Yahoola Creek is the single most gold-storied creek in the district — an 1830 Niles' Register report cited ~4,000 miners working the creek, and the Dahlonega Consolidated Gold Mining Co. built its stamp mill (reportedly largest east of the Mississippi) on its banks.
pressure: Low for panning specifically — locals use the park for disc golf, trails, sports fields; tourists go to the museum instead.
target_tips: Creek-adjacent picnic areas along the park; look for gravel bars away from the mowed lawn frontage.

photos.credit: Wikimedia Commons, panoramio import — see file page for author/license

notes: Call ahead to confirm panning is still a tolerated park activity (evidence is TripAdvisor reviews + secondary sources, not a county ordinance).

name: Tesnatee Creek at Tesnatee Gap
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, node 10154264141 'Tesnatee Gap', Union County GA
access: Richard B. Russell Scenic Hwy (GA-348) east from Vogel/Neel Gap to Tesnatee Gap; roadside pull-off at the gap, short walk down to Tesnatee Creek along Town Creek Rd/AT crossing area.
legality: USFS Chattahoochee NF general forest, not Wilderness. Tesnatee Creek is a tributary of the Chestatee River.
gold_record: Several old mine sites documented nearby in the Dahlonega belt district literature; specific site-level mine name not pulled this pass.
pressure: Low; mostly AT thru-hikers pass through, few stop to pan.
target_tips: Closest option to Vogel geographically — good for a short first/last-day session.

photos.credit: Wikimedia Commons, panoramio import — see file page for author/license

notes: Very close to camp — good low-commitment first-afternoon stop.

name: Dukes Creek Falls Recreation Area (NF trail, not Smithgall Woods)
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, way 240073969 'Dukes Creek Falls', White County GA (trailhead/parking area)
access: GA-75 S then Richard Russell/Dukes Creek Rd (FS 44 spur) to the Dukes Creek Falls trailhead. $4/vehicle/day USFS parking fee. 2.5-mile round-trip moderate trail with overlook platforms; leave the maintained trail to reach the creek itself well below/above the falls (steep terrain — falls area itself is not a panning spot).
legality: USFS Chattahoochee NF — this is the National Forest side of the Dukes Creek drainage, upstream of and separate from the privately-managed Smithgall Woods State Park / Dukes Creek Gold & Ruby Mines commercial tract further downstream. General-forest panning rule applies here; do NOT cross into Smithgall Woods (state park, mineral extraction banned) or onto the commercial mine's posted land.
gold_record: Dukes Creek is ground zero for the 1828-29 Georgia Gold Rush discovery legend (Benjamin Parks / Frank Logan / John Witheroods accounts, all undocumented contemporaneously); historic reports include large nuggets and several pre-Civil-War mines on the creek.
pressure: Moderate — popular waterfall hike draws hikers, but almost none leave the boardwalk/overlook to pan the creek itself.
target_tips: Above the falls trailhead parking, working upstream away from the platform crowds; watch footing, steep terrain.
fees: $4/vehicle/day USFS parking fee at the trailhead.

photos.credit: Wikimedia Commons — see file page for author/license

notes: Do not confuse with Smithgall Woods State Park (excluded, see smithgall-dukes entry) — verify the NF/state-park boundary on a map before leaving the trail.

legality: Mixed — upper Coosa Creek sits near/within Chattahoochee NF and Coosa Bald National Scenic Area (not statutory Wilderness, panning likely allowed per FAQ inference, per prior verification.md item 3 — flagged lower-confidence, call Blue Ridge RD to confirm). The lower-valley historic mine site near Blairsville proper may be on private or mixed land — UNVERIFIED.
gold_record: Coosa Mine (thediggings.com ID usgs10240673): described in Union Co. mining histories as the most famous mine in the county, run on a business-like basis, with reports of over $2 million in gold recovered historically.
pressure: Low — not a tourist-known name like Dukes/Consolidated.
target_tips: Treat as an exploratory stop; verify exact legal public reach before digging in.

name: Wolf Creek / Auraria historic mining cluster
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, node 4322550469 'Auraria' historic marker, Castleberry Bridge Rd, Lumpkin County GA — this is the ghost-town center, not a specific creek-access point
access: Castleberry Bridge Rd / Auraria Rd area SW of Dahlonega. Exact public creek-frontage pull-off not confirmed this pass — treat as a walk-in exploratory stop near the ghost town; verify public vs. private frontage before digging.

gold_record: Auraria was a rival boomtown to Dahlonega in the 1830s; historic mines nearby include Battle Branch Mine, Barlow Mine, Ralston Mine, Whim Hill Mine along the Etowah River, Camp Creek, Cane Creek and Wolf Creek per Auraria-history sources.
pressure: Low.

name: Upper Chestatee River at US-19 bridge

access: US-19 south of Dahlonega; roadside pull-off near the bridge, short scramble down to a wide gravel bar.
legality: Road ROW / adjacent gravel bar — widely used, treat as an established public access point.

name: Waters Creek / Dicks Creek (Chestatee WMA, outside trophy-water boundary)
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, node 7589425216 'Dicks Creek Falls', Lumpkin County GA

Merrill Ranger Station with artificial-lures-only fishing rules; whether non-angler panning is separately restricted inside the managed trophy section is UNVERIFIED. Pan only water clearly outside that boundary, e.g. Dicks Creek itself away from the trophy stretch, or call ahead.
gold_record: District-level Dahlonega belt gold record; no site-specific ledger pulled.
pressure: Moderate (well-known waterfall/trophy-trout name draws hikers and anglers), but panning-specific pressure is low since visitors come for the falls/fish, not gold.
target_tips: Stick to Dicks Creek proper away from the trophy-water signage.
fees: WMA stamp/check-in required if entering the trophy-water section; none for general forest access.
notes: Carried over from prior research — legal status of non-angler panning inside the WMA boundary remains UNVERIFIED; call GA DNR Gainesville office before relying on this spot.

name: LDMA Loud Mine Camp
stream: Unnamed branch, Loud Creek/Dukes Creek watershed vicinity
coord_source: OSM Nominatim, way 9542011 'Abb Helton Road', White County GA (road centroid near the claim's 575 Abb Helton Rd address; not the exact gate)
access: 575 Abb Helton Rd, Cleveland, GA 30528 (5 mi from Cleveland). LDMA (Lost Dutchman's Mining Association) claim on the Loud Mine property, 37 acres in the Dahlonega gold belt with documented stream gold and bench deposits.
legality: Private club claim — LDMA membership normally required for routine access; the club's public 'Gold Diggin's Spooktacular' event Oct 13-17, 2026 is open to the public (paid registration, capped at 75 participants) and overlaps the first two days of this trip window.
gold_record: Marketed by LDMA as rich stream gold and bench-deposit ground in the historic Dahlonega belt.
pressure: Managed/controlled — club claim, not open streambed.
target_tips: Different tool rules likely apply than NF streambeds (may allow sluice/highbank on a club claim) — confirm equipment rules for the specific event.
fees: Public event requires paid registration (amount not confirmed this pass); LDMA annual membership otherwise required for routine access.
notes: Time-sensitive: the public Spooktacular event (Oct 13-17) only overlaps Oct 15-17 of this trip — call LDMA to confirm event access/fee before counting on this.

access: 1 Public Square, Dahlonega town square. Museum only — housed in the old Lumpkin County Courthouse.

gold_record: Interprets the 1828-29 gold rush, the 1838-1861 Dahlonega Branch Mint ($6M+ in gold coins struck), and mining history.
pressure: High (major tourist draw) but it's an indoor museum, doesn't compete with creek panning spots.
target_tips: Good rainy-day or arrival-day stop before heading to the creeks.
fees: Standard GA state historic site admission (parking pass).
notes: Mon-Sat 9am-4:45pm, Sun 10am-4:45pm; closed Thanksgiving/Christmas/New Year's.
